newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey invites IMF, prepares medium-term plan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey invites IMF, prepares medium-term plan.

text.p: Turkey has officially invited International Monetary Fund (IMF) officials for talks in late March or early April and has set up a committee to draw up a three-year plan to reduce inflation, State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said on Monday.

"I wrote an invitation letter to IMF president Michael Camdessus, asking them to bring forward their visit scheduled for May to late March or early April," Soylemez, in charge of treasury and privatisation, told reporters.

Turkish bankers have urged the government to reach a new stand-by accord with the IMF and prepare a medium-term stabilisation programme to narrow big public deficits, estimated at over 10 percent of gross national product.

Soylemez said the government ministers had agreed in principle to hammer out a three-year economic programme to reduce inflation, running at around 85 percent annually, and tackle other problems of the ailing economy.

"We have set up a committee of officials from the central bank, treasury, state planning organisation and finanace ministry. Our aim is to bring the inflation down through a three-year economic programme," he said.
But he said the programme would not be ready before an IMF team arrives in a month's time. "The programme is not for the IMF anyway. It is for us," he said.
Details on the programme would be determined after the economic council of senior government ministers has given the official go-ahead for the committee's work, he said.
He said the government would seek IMF support on the basis of its performance in the first three months of this year.

"We had told them in November that we would speed up privatisations, submit the draft law on the social security system to parliament, lower interest rates and extend maturities (of domestic borrowing) and not allow reserves to fall below $15-$16 billion," he said.
"We are happy we have achieved all these and we will show them our performance and ask them to carry on with international support in getting credits," he said.
He said the IMF support did not have to be through a stand-by accord. "I think the talks will be positive," he said.
The IMF was due to come to Turkey in February but the visit was postponed. Officials did not give any reason for the postponement.
